findings.message: The ticket requires soft-spiral and stuck trips to page through 'the existing notification transport as an Effect' on both bootstrap drain and serve, with 'Configured transport, unset status-only behavior and notification replay' green. On main only `_serve` builds `SubprocessNotifications`. Only `Serve.compose` builds the `NotificationReconciler`, and it runs at startup and on each watcher poll. `_drain` and `Drain` build neither, and `NotificationReconciler._escalations` only knows storm_trip and integration_red_streak signals. The ticket also forbids sending from the provider callback. So on drain a journaled watchdog trip signal is never delivered, and the ticket does not say whether drain gains a transport and reconcile point, or whether drain trips stay status-only.
findings.paved_road: State the drain notification contract explicitly. Either (a) `_drain` builds the same `SubprocessNotifications`/config.notify transport and drain runs `NotificationReconciler.reconcile` at a named point (for example after each dispatch and at startup), with its unset warning; or (b) drain trips are journaled as signals and are status-only until serve, with the drain criterion changed to match. In either case, say that `NotificationReconciler._escalations` gains the watchdog soft and stuck identities, keyed ticket+spiral+run_seq and ticket+stuck.

findings.message: Nothing says how a soft or stuck trip reaches the reconciler. The only escalation producer the reconciler reads is a journal signal, and the ticket forbids a synchronous send from the callback, yet it never names the signal kind or body the binding appends. That makes the migration of `tests/test_notify.py::test_unrelated_signals_and_hold_release_do_not_notify` conditional ('if the new recognized signal uses it') and leaves no pinned interface for the notify criteria.
findings.paved_road: Name the journal signal the binding appends on a soft trip and on stuck (kind and body fields: ticket, spiral, run_seq), and say whether it reuses `kind: watchdog`. If it does, make the notify-test migration unconditional, and still prove that an unrecognized watchdog-kind body does not notify.

findings.message: Scope in compares 'normalized metered spend' against '3 x the serving-row per-call cost basis' but never says what unit either side is in. WatchdogEvent carries both `usd` and `input_tokens`/`output_tokens`, and the ticket forbids a token-to-USD conversion. It does not say whether a tokens-only event counts as metered spend, whether the cost basis is USD or tokens, or how an event carrying both is normalized. The 'flat estimate' charged at a non-metered provider's start event is also not among the enumerated injected inputs, and 'provider without metered usage' is not defined in terms of WatchdogEvent fields. An implementer must pick a unit and a metered/flat classification, and the Definition of rejected already rejects 'invented cost conversion'.
findings.paved_road: State the spend unit and its source field exactly. For example: the cost basis is an injected USD float; metered spend sums `WatchdogEvent.usd` when present; token counts are retained but never compared. Name the flat per-call estimate as an explicit injected detector input with the same unit. Define 'provider without metered usage' mechanically, for example an injected per-provider flag, or 'no event of the invocation carries usd'. Add an acceptance assertion for a tokens-only stream under that definition.
